subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should Mattermost native slash command registration fail closed for any non-HTTPS callback URL before this PR can merge?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but it intentionally breaks existing HTTP callback deployments while tightening a reusable-token transport boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent policy alone.

options.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed
options.body: Accept the security hardening after real Mattermost proof, PR refresh, and explicit maintainer/security sign-off.

options.title: Stage the compatibility change
options.body: Ask for a compatibility design such as a documented migration window or opt-in strict mode before breaking HTTP callback deployments.

options.title: Pause this PR
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and replace this branch if maintainers want a different transport policy or upgrade path.

recommendation.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed
recommendation.body: Accept the security hardening after real Mattermost proof, PR refresh, and explicit maintainer/security sign-off.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Mattermost monitor and slash-validation history makes this the best available routing owner for the callback transport policy choice.
